grid.pasteLabel: Paste the copied table here (⌘+V on Mac, Ctrl+V on Windows)
grid.pastePlaceholder: e.g. select the range with headers in Excel, copy, and paste here
grid.pasteNone: Could not read a table. Paste tab-separated data (a copy from Excel).
clarify.heading: A few quick questions
clarify.lead: Your description doesn’t tell us enough to pick a way to show it. Choose what fits and we’ll suggest angles.
unsupported.heading: We can’t make a chart for this yet
unsupported.body: Charts for “{goal}” (scorecards across several metrics) are not ready yet, and we won’t force a near match. You can also start from a purpose or a chart.
grid.sample: This is sample data. Type over it or replace it with “Paste from Excel”.
grid.yearsAcross: Years run across the columns. Trend charts need years in the rows.
grid.transposed: Rows and columns were swapped so that years are in the rows.
grid.baseHidden: Show the comparison-period table (not used by these slides)
history.label: Undo and redo
fit.mekko_time: The rows are years. A Mekko compares size and mix at one point; with years as widths they get re-sorted by size and the flow of time is lost.
fit.line_not_time: The rows are not time periods. A line implies a flow over time, so connecting separate items can mislead.
fit.non_additive_stack: The unit is “{unit}”. Rates, averages and indices cannot be added up, so stacked or share charts do not fit.
fit.many_columns: There are {n} items. Their names will be hard to read in a column chart.
fit.many_lines: There are {n} lines — too many to read. Highlight one, or narrow the rows and columns shown.
fit.negative_share: Some values are negative. A 100% share chart cannot show negative values.
fit.heading: How this data fits the chart
field.dimensionsHint: Used for the table’s corner heading and for legend and table headings (e.g. rows = year, columns = region).
needs.DRIVER_BRIDGE: First row = start, last row = end, rows in between = drivers (first column)
needs.BUBBLE: Rows = items × column 1 = X, column 2 = Y (column 3 = size)
fit.bridge_one_col: Driver charts use only the first column ({col}): first row = start, last row = end, rows between = drivers.
fit.relation_cols: Relationship charts read column 1 as X and column 2 as Y (and column 3 as size for bubbles). Add at least two numeric columns.
rechoose.title: None of these? Pick by what you want to show
rechoose.lead: Choose an angle here without asking again (no usage counted).
rechoose.fromUnsupported: You can still pick a close way to show it from “None of these?” below.
feedback.question: Were these suggestions helpful?
feedback.reason.not_my_goal: Not what I want to show
feedback.commentLabel: Comment (optional): how did you want to show it?
feedback.commentPlaceholder: e.g. I wanted a bubble chart of growth vs margin by product
feedback.thanks: We’ll use your feedback to improve the service.
feedback.error: Could not send. Please try again later.
feedback.privacy: The current page path is sent too. Your data and consultation text are not sent automatically.
suggest.heading: With this data, you could also
suggest.items_two_metrics: Each item has two numeric measures. To show how they relate or where items sit, a scatter plot fits.
suggest.items_three_metrics: Each item has three numeric measures. To add size to a relationship, a bubble chart fits (column 1 = X, 2 = Y, 3 = size).
suggest.single_col_changes: One column mixes positive and negative values. For drivers from a start to an end value, a waterfall fits.
suggest.years_rows: The rows are years. To show change over time, a line chart fits.
fit.relation_years: The columns are years. Scatter and bubble charts use two or three measures per item (e.g. growth, margin, sales) as X, Y and size. For change over years, a line chart fits.
section.dataSharedN: Data (shared by {n} slides of this shape)
consult.fallback.limit: (you have used this month’s AI allowance)
grid.copied: Copied. You can paste it into Excel or Sheets.
grid.copyFailed: Could not copy. Check your browser settings.
grid.pasteKinds: You can paste a wide table (rows × columns) or a long table (one value per line, e.g. year · region · type · value). The first line is used as headers.
grid.longDetected: This looks like a long table (headers: {cols}, {n} lines). Choose “Read as a long table” to pick rows, columns and filters for the chart table.
grid.longAsWide: Read as a wide table as is
grid.longHint: This table is cut from a long table (not editable here). To change numbers, fix the source and paste again, or choose “Stop and edit directly” above.
long.title: Cut from a long table
long.intro: The chart table below is built from the source table ({n} lines). Change the choices and the table and chart update right away.
long.rowNote: For trends, choose a time column such as year
long.filterAllNote: “{name}” is not split; all are added up
long.calcNote: Choose share to see percentages. It is calculated per cell, and the unit becomes %.
long.calcNoFilter: To get a share, filter one column to a single value (e.g. type = steam).
long.totalNote: Adds a column with the sum of each row. Do not use it if the values are already % or averages.
long.totalShareNote: The total share adds the amounts first, then divides (not an average of “{name}” percentages; larger ones weigh more).
long.merged: {n} lines had the same combination and were added up. A filter may be missing (e.g. Vol and Val mixed).
long.empty: {n} cells are empty because the share’s denominator is 0.
long.detachNote: The current table stays; the source table and choices are removed.
long.perSlide: Each slide can have its own choices. To show Vol and Val on separate slides, use “Duplicate” on the left and change the filter.
entry.ai.history: When signed in, your requests are kept in “Request history” on My page (only you can see them, and you can delete them).
history.note: Your requests are kept, newest first, up to {n}. Starred ones stay even beyond {n}. Only you can see them.
history.empty: No requests yet. Ask from “New” and they will appear here.
history.openChart: Open the chart made from this request
history.error: Could not load the request history ({message}). Check that the history table exists in Supabase.
long.melted: The number columns ({cols}) were stacked into one column “{name}”. Choose share within “{name}” to get, for example, the share of {first} ({first} ÷ all {name}).
long.compare: Compare two points in time (base and current)
long.compareNote: For charts that use two points (base and current), such as the paired 100% stacked chart, Mekko comparison or change labels. The earlier point goes into the “Base” tab below.
long.needsCompare: This chart uses two points (base and current). Turn on “Compare two points in time” below and choose them.
long.selfPercent: This chart turns values into % itself, so “As is” is recommended (a share here would become a % of %).
long.filterTimeNote: Only one point is used. To show two points,
long.compareUnused: This chart uses only the current point ({current}); the base ({base}) is not shown. To compare the mix at two points for each item, use the paired 100% stacked chart.
long.toSharePair: Switch to the paired 100% stacked chart

beta.lead: Slide Story Coach is in beta. Join with your email to get, for free:

beta.terms.t1: The beta is for trying the service. Features may change or stop, and data may be removed, without notice.

beta.terms.t5: To leave the beta or delete your data, contact us (the address is in our announcement emails).

confirm.slideBody:
This slide’s title, chart and view settings will be removed. The data is shared with other slides and stays.
Right after, you can restore it with Undo.
confirm.rowColBody:
Its values are removed from both current and base. Other slides using the same data are affected too.
Right after, you can restore it with Undo.
confirm.resetBody:
This slide’s data, title and settings will be replaced by the sample.
Right after, you can restore it with Undo.
confirm.detachTitle: Stop cutting from the long table?
confirm.detachBody: The source long table and your choices will be removed (the current table stays and becomes editable). To cut again, paste the table again.
confirm.chartBody: All saved versions and data will be removed. This cannot be undone.
confirm.historyBody:
“{text}”
This cannot be undone (charts you made are kept).
confirm.libraryTitle: Delete the example “{name}” from the Library?
confirm.libraryBody: The example will be removed for everyone. This cannot be undone. To keep it, use “Hide” instead (copies people already made are kept).
